Hi Anna — thanks for the screenshot and flagging this. You're hitting a bug we've seen when customers open our Calendly/Chili Piper widget from a browser with a non-local locale. The scheduling widget sometimes renders in the visitor's detected timezone but the confirmation email uses the server or cookie timezone, which causes the mismatch.

Short-term workaround I'd like to propose so everyone has a clean calendar invite:
- Can you confirm which timezone the Berlin attendees want the calendar in (CET/CEST) and whether Tokyo participants should see the invite in JST?
- We'll send a manual .ics invite from our side set to the agreed timezone (so your calendar won't auto-shift).
- We'll include the time in the subject/body in two zones (CET / JST) and place the Zoom link in the body (so copies in different calendar systems still show the same link).

I've attached a quick timezone matrix for common cross-region viewings (timezone-matrix.csv) to help pick a time that keeps the meeting inside working hours for both offices. If you prefer, propose 16:00 CET and I can push an invite now.

I'll also loop in Vivek for any technical prep. Apologies for the friction — we'll make sure the invite you receive matches the confirmed slot.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor

Thanks — quick clarification from Tokyo side. When Anna clicked the link earlier it showed 09:00 but in our machines that was JST. For us 09:00 JST would be 01:00 CET which is not workable.

We agree that 16:00 CET / 00:00 JST is also outside Tokyo hours. Could we do 14:00 CET (22:00 JST) is still late. Best overlap for both is 16:00 CET (00:00 JST) is bad, so we'd prefer 08:00 CET (16:00 JST) or 15:00 CET (23:00 JST) — both are tight. If the Berlin crew prefer afternoon, perhaps 10:00 CET (18:00 JST) is the compromise.

Anna — does 10:00 CET work?
